newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to amend law to reveal loan defaulters.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to amend law to reveal loan defaulters.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker cabinet will amend banking laws to enable the government to publish a list of bank defaulters ahead of general elections set for February 3, Information Minister Irshad Haqqani said on Monday.

He told a news conference President Farooq Leghari would issue an ordinance in the next few days to remove legal obstacles in the way of publicising the names of those who had defaulted on loans or had them cancelled.
Haqqani said the ordinance had no specific targets. "We have not taken this decision keeping in mind a person or any particular political party," he said.
Leghari said last week that new electoral laws had ensured that politicians would have to declare they were not loan defaulters before being allowed to contest the elections.
An estimated 6,000 people had defaulted on loans exceeding half a million rupees, he said, adding that those who repaid their loans would become eligible to stand in the polls.
Pakistani banks have a combined portfolio of up to 130 billion rupees in bad loans, bankers say.
